title: I Will Make Your Name Great

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "I will make you into a great nation, and I will bless you; I will make your name great, and you will be a blessing." - Gen 12:2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Look at the pronouns in this verse: I will, I will, I will. Everything depends on God. At Babel, humanity said "let us make a name for ourselves" - and it ended in confusion and scattering. Now God says to one man, "I will make your name great." What people grasped at in pride, God gives freely as a gift.

This is the difference between building and receiving. Babel built upward in self-effort; Abram simply received a promise. And notice the impossibility of it - God promises a "great nation" to a man whose wife cannot have children (Gen 11:30). The promise rests entirely on God's power, not Abram's ability.

But see where the blessing points: "you will be a blessing." God's blessing is never meant to terminate on us. He blesses us so that we become a channel of blessing to others. Abram was chosen not for privilege but for purpose.

That is still how God works. He does not bless us so we can hoard His goodness, but so it can flow through us to a watching world. Whatever God has given you - resources, gifts, opportunities, faith itself - He has given it to make you a blessing. Stop striving to make your own name great. Receive what God gives, and let it flow outward.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Are you trying to build your name, or receiving what God gives?
- How is God's blessing in your life meant to flow through you to others?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, forgive me for grasping at greatness. Thank You that You give freely what I could never build. Make me a channel of Your blessing to others, not a container that keeps it.
Amen.
